parsed_response.reasoning: Verified in the diff: `createEvent(credential, calEvent, externalId?)` accepts the routed destination's externalId but only uses it as a pass-through in the return object (`externalId,` added to the result), never forwarding it to `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)`. Meanwhile `createAllCalendarEvents` loops over all destination calendars for collective events, but Lark/Office365/BaseCalendarService each added `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []` fallbacks that always select the first array element regardless of which destination/credential is being processed. For multi-host collective bookings this means non-Google providers write every event to the first host's calendar (or 'primary'), and the externalId needed for correct routing exists but is not plumbed through the Calendar interface. The mechanism described is accurate and grounded; whether the misrouting manifests as a hard defect depends on runtime data, so confidence is moderate.

judged_text: createEvent accepts the routed destination's externalId but forwards only `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)` — the externalId is used solely as a pass-through return value, so no service other than Google (which re-derives the target via credentialId) can know which calendar it was asked to write to. Each provider had to invent its own fallback (the mainHost destructures in Lark/Office365/BaseCalendarService that break multi-host); forwarding the already-routed destination.externalId through the Calendar interface this PR already changed would delete those three divergent workarounds and make multi-host behavior provider-agnostic.

Each provider had to invent its own fallback (the mainHost destructures in Lark/Office365/BaseCalendarService that break multi-host); forwarding the already-routed destination.externalId through the Calendar interface this PR already changed would delete those three divergent workarounds and make multi-host behavior provider-agnostic.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `CalendarManager.createEvent(credential, calEvent, externalId?)` receives a per-destination `externalId` from `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` (`createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)`), but then calls `calendar.createEvent(calEvent, credential.id)` and never forwards/uses `externalId` for routing. Non-Google providers in this diff then select the target calendar by destructuring the *first* destination (`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = event.destinationCalendar ?? []`) and using `mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId` (e.g., Lark/Office365/BaseCalendarService), which will be wrong when `event.destinationCalendar` contains multiple entries (multi-host / collective), causing events to be created/filtered against the first calendar regardless of which destination is being processed. Only Google re-derives selection via `credentialId` (`find(cal => cal.credentialId === credentialId)`), so other providers cannot reliably know which calendar they were asked to write to.
